reviews.text: Having about 300h in playtest before this release, this is a huge imrovement over IEH1 and one of the best idlers ive played (ive played IdleOn, Idle champion, Melvor etc). If youre the type that likes gradual automation and RPG elements, different heroes, gear, pets and so on i highly recommend it. Lots of fun systems that dont require a ton of micromanaging (which i personally dont like in other idlers) and more systems / endgame / updates on the way. Theres no p2w bs, the DLC is just an initial boost and you can get the premium currency yourself with daily quests anyways. Theres no multiplayer aspect so its just your own solo progress. The people who said its p2w simply have little to no playtime and have no idea what theyre talking about. You literally unlock every QoL and automation in the game by progressing through the world, pets and daily quests that give you premium currency. You can obtain everything by playing the game, the DLC only gives you extra currency to start with and buy some QoL earlier which btw you cant even use because you cant progress fast enough for it to really matter. As in you need to first unlock x feature by playing the game to use x qol and you wont unlock that faster with money and by the time you can use all the qol you will have most of them from dailies. In the end it just takes time, like all idle games. And even if you spend all the money in the world you wont really progress much faster, all youll get is having less micromanaging somewhat earlier. The beginning can be a bit slow if youre a new player (because you might not be sure what to focus on) but the further you progress the more straightforward and automated everything becomes and then you set it and forget it. Lastly the classes and heroes are very well balanced allowing you to play w/e you want but you can basically switch anytime regardless. Wizard is the coolest though.

Very good slow paced incremental game, similar to Trimps, NGU Idle, Leaf Blower, etc. Not supposed to be completed in a few days. Of course you can speed through this game by paying money but it is an offline game, so it should not matter how outrageous you think the cash shop is, just experience the game how it is meant to be played. Anyone complaining about monetization or slow pacing is not an idle player. 99% of cash shop rewards are able to be earned F2P eventually.
Just the same garbage as IEH1. Where 99% of the QoL features of an incremental are hidden behind real money currency.

So, the game is fun. It starts out incredibly slow, mainly because the Rebirth mechanic that his genre is known for, takes roughly 20 hours of active play to unlock, whereas other Idle games introduce you to a brick wall in the first couple hours and answer that by teaching you how to Rebirth. However, once you perform that first Rebirth, things do significantly speed up. It's also one of the more complex games, even for an Idler, with just an absolutely ton of customization and advancement. Literally everything in this game has some form of upgrade, and there are dozens of mechanics that intermingle with the others in some way. To add to this, you have 6 classes, which can learn each others moves on the fly. The game has a Cash Shop, but nothing there is game breaking, and more importantly, can be earned overtime through ingame grind (usually through daily quests). There's a lot to do here, and even though it's an idler, it can be somewhat played actively. I was genuinely having a blast with this game... until I found out about World Ascension. World Ascension basically deletes your account, and starts you over with a slight advantage. It's sort of like the Rebirth mechanic of other games you've played, but for your Account. However, unlocking this takes literal weeks and is counter-intuitive to what the game is trying to accomplish. Everything you do in this game is slow, with the effort of slowly increases your progress with each Rebirth and game mechanic, with the ultimate goal of an efficient and swift longterm endgame. World Ascension absolutely craps all over this, by deleting almost all of your progress, with the hopes of a slightly faster playthrough, making playing the game utterly pointless. It's basically NG+, but before you even finished the game and you don't get keep anything you spend a thousand hours grinding for. You do seem to keep some things, but none of the more time intense activities or anything that's going to have a huge impact on the speed of your next playthrough. Why bother picking up that equipment, when it's going to get deleted? Why bother leveling and training your skills, when all of your characters are getting deleted? Why bother exploring the world and hunting down those ultra rare items that have less than a 1% droprate, when your going to permanently lose it? Someone on the forums tried to defend World Ascension to me, by explaining that it took them 2 weeks to unlock it, and they earned their progress back in 5 days... However, what I'm hearing is that it took them 3 weeks of grind to make 1 week of progress, which is incredibly stupid. Ever since I found out that this mechanic is waiting for me, any enjoyment I had got sucked out of the game. I can't bother doing anything in the game, since nothing I do matters in the long run. Eventually, the game even plays itself, so there's not much of a reason to even bother play, since none of my personal choices or effort matters. It's a shame, because if you completely ignore the World Ascension, it's an absolutely interesting game, worth playing if your a fan of idlers, but I just can't be bothered, knowing that literally nothing I do now will matters hundreds of hours later, since I'll have to do it all over again. After finding out about World Ascension, the game went from being the funnest I've played in a while, to disgusting me in literal minutes. Imagine playing an MMO, like FF14 or Warframe, but after a 1,000 hours you logged in to find that your characters and mounts were all deleted, all your raid gear was gone, along with your money and resources, but the game promises that if you keep playing, this time around you'll get +25% experience! Would you bother wasting your life playing that game, knowing that even if you bother to suffer through another 1,000 hours, your going to have to do this again several dozen more times for very little gain or personal fun?

===================总的来说是很好玩儿的放置类游戏============================ 退游前总结，如果没玩儿过IEH1的朋友，初期劲量多用金币攒点高级商店里的“贿赂IEH升阶成就”牌子，名字可能有误，效果是*110%经验提升，20个效果是*300%.能保证在WA1前8小时拿到3-11个升阶成就.并且在WA0世界,这算是增幅最大的项目之一了.相当于不低于300级转生经验加成. 指数增长游戏里，（1+N）^M提升3倍[(1+N)*3]^M，差的可不是简单的3倍。 ==以下是我之前的一些不愉快体验,新玩家加入时可能已经改正不会遇到,请喜欢游戏的玩家酌情参考,不可尽信==== 好游戏，但是有个现象我提一句。 官方交流群里有个标准攻略，但是这个攻略里埋着一个陷阱，就是“收集20个IEH1升阶证明”这个是攻略成立的所有前提，失去这个提前，整个攻略反而会变成新人坟墓，变成禁放置，禁育成，甚至3个月都无法达到攻略基本要求，已经不是新人交流QQ群了，是坑杀新人来获取优越感的陷阱了。 还在各大宣传平台，用同样的方式，嘲讽其他不愿意修改的人和UP自己摸索的方法。修改的核心却只字不提。有异议，有改良的意见全部按闹事处理，实际上闹事的人是他们吧？毫无体验可言。 请这样的人群来宣传，作者是真心实意希望自己的作品没人接触么？ ============后续============ https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Da411377z/?vd_source=1a74703c8aa9f702d183b7da9700f62d#reply131674490032 就这么会儿功夫，我从“开变速”“新人”“低效率”“不懂游戏机制导致打了差评”，又多了“偏执”“排外”“傲慢”“自我”“不够包容”这些标签 游戏才发售2个月，接触晚点WA0加成很少，全按8秒过图算，图都不一定开完了。14件万分之一的稀有装备都不一定凑齐。 玩个游戏而已，还玩这套？累了，已卸游。再也不见。 ==========================写在退游前夕======================= 好游戏，林子大了什么鸟都有，日本作者给我回复用词还是很正常。我不知道这人什么目的，也不想知道。 玩个游戏而已，还玩这套？累了，已卸游。再也不见。 祝： 认真工作的小组制作出更好的游戏。 玩家在游戏里畅享制作小组创造的有趣的世界。

tl;dr - Don't be a moron like me, steer clear from this game - in fact, avoid any trash with premium shops/DLC no matter what. Past several months I've gotten into various idle games. Been playing Melvor Idle for over 6 months. While I'm a fan of the genre, seems I had a lesson to learn and this game was a good teacher. Initially the Epic Coin shop was a little disappointing to see, but I gave it a chance primarily because I didn't understand the mechanics and purpose of the upgrades. As I got more invested in the game, I learned how important those items in the Epic Coin shop were for convenience and progress. Bit by bit, bought more and more to maintain decent automation and QoL. And here I am now writing this review - quite a bit of money spent and regret my time, effort and money spent. Let me elaborate. 'Early Access' - classic dogwater crap you'd expect. Dev abandonded the game for the forseeable future. Last update was in May, not even a hotfix since. Lots of unfinished things with placeholders, lots of things that you think exist until you realize they don't. Virtually pointless after 'end game' - can buy out the shop like me and spend 2 months getting to the end to realize the next features are yet to be implemented and just have placeholders. Nothing to do, considering it's an idle game, this shouldn't happen unless the game has a deliberate end or deliberate final goal to focus on long term. Money spent and the cucks defending the daily quests for Epic Coins - just ignore these drooling dribbling test player shills. Yeah sure, you can buy out the shop by getting the addtional quest + rarity upgrades and saving for weeks to get a feature that SHOULD BE IMPLEMENTED BY DEFAULT. How do these people function in society financially? 'Yeah bro, college costs money but if you pick up a night shift job at McDons for 8$ an hour you can eventually get there..', 'No man you're wrong, if you scrounge the streets to pick up change off the ground near Walmart, you can even replace your grocery budget!' Piss off lmao Further on the topic of money - this whole concept of free, early access, premium shop, microtransaction, etc stuff is just sad. It's a manipulative excuse for a business model nothing more than that. It's not an 'alternative' way to sell a game, take this is an example: Game A --- Spend $20 for the game. Have access to everything in the game. Potentially have access to mods that let you modify the game or change how fast progress happens. That's it Game B --- FREE game! Can spend between $0 and $2,500 depending on disposable income. Have access to certain features, partial features, and how fast you progress as a function of money spent in the premium shop or 'DLC'. Mods are forbidden as they damage and rob these oh so, hard working honest developers by invalidating their manipulative business model. Certain tactics used to increase both likelihood of playing longer and likelihood of spending more money such as daily rewards, making large gaps between parts of the game closeable through a small purchase, intentionally making features annoying/tedious with a small purchase relieving the issue, bundling DLC with (focus on the C) financial incentives, just straight up presenting DLC as a financial incentive with no content, etc. If you didn't get the point - Game A is a game being sold in the framework of an honest, fair model. You spend money and get everything as advertised instead of having everything littered with traps and attempts to induce small purchases repetitively, and many metaphorical 'well, ACKTUALLY ...' used as a defense. Game B is a dishonest, manipulative framework for generating sales disguised as a game. If you still don't get it, go back to shining the dev's boots with your tongue. I will admit the mechanics of the game are top notch - a lot of choices and flexibility, strategy, decision-making, planning, management, etc. pulled off really well. Unfortunately instead of slapping a price tag on it of like 15 or even 30$, the devs gotta act a lil shady to fund his sex toy collection. That's all. Don't be a moron like me and avoid this game. Avoid any game using premium shops or paywalls features/progress. Unless you're a financial cuck, then its all cool

快跑！！！作为一款放置游戏，数值设计和游戏系统自动化方面烂得一塌糊涂。 重生与升阶的提升与付出相比简直太微不足道，很难提供数值积累的爽感，特别是升阶后的强大落差感和挫败感。 很多理所当然的游戏内容被拆成付费内容销售，那我更倾向于买断制，虽然可以通过每日任务慢慢攒，但是这不就变成上班性质了么。并且很大一部分的游戏内容并不完善，即使到了游戏后期也只能达到半自动的程度，前期各种系统需要的手动操作不胜其烦，能够解锁的自动系统只不过杯水车薪。 游戏汉化体验很好，在此感谢汉化的哥们或是工作室，但是为什么不顺带把成就汉化一下。总结，虽然是一款免费放置游戏，但是需要大量的时间和操作，快跑！！！ 写完逛了一下评论区，发现还是有一些值得参考的评论，但是这并不能改变我的意见，一款游戏不应该以十天半个月为期限折磨玩家来告诉你说这是前期积累，并且作为一款小众的放置类游戏（应该算是），更不应该告诉玩家说你感到痛苦是因为你没玩懂。 最后，如果你有大量的时间和心力了解这个游戏复杂的系统和操作，能够有氪金的条件或是每天上线打卡的毅力并且对于这款游戏度过前期（开始感到愉快之前）后得到的数值积累快感保持期待，这会是一款好游戏。 对于我个人而言，初高中可能会很喜欢这个游戏，但是我现在更想要更直接爽快的打打杀杀或是赛上一场飞车。如果我说的这些不合你胃口，那就，快跑！！！

An idle RPG focused on long-term progression through skills, classes, gear, and incremental upgrades. The early and mid-game are very strong, with a wide variety of skills and classes that feel distinct, along with interesting gear that provides meaningful goals to work toward. However, the progression begins to break down around later stages, where the game becomes significantly more grind-heavy and less rewarding. Monetization plays a major role in this decline, with many quality-of-life features and meaningful progression tied to paid currency that is difficult to earn through normal play. Eventually, the game stops feeling like a true idle experience and becomes more of an active grind, while also losing the satisfying sense of progression that defined its early game. Overall: Strong start with a disappointing late-game decline (2.8/5)

Fun and unique idle game! I wanted to address criticism saying this game requires purchases/grinding in its endgame. In the world of Free Incremental games it's not uncommon to see a Premium shop. Devs normally provide players one or two years of free gameplay, during which you're given the ability to gain enough Premium currency to buy out said shop's most important items for free. You're not expected to grind out the rest of the items unless you wish to support the Dev's free game. Examples: NGU, Wizard Wheel 2, ITRTG are all successful, loved games of this genre with the same endgame. Progression in this game/Incremental Epic Hero 2 feels fun, there are soo many quests, mechanics and classes to unlock (all at a good pace). Prestige feels rewarding and the game has features not present in many other idles, ie. the switchable classes actually interact with each other so you can play all of them at once and manage a party like a typical RPG. The graphics are also overall super charming! I've been satisfied with what I've played thus far and I think other incremental fans will be too. It's definitely a fun addition to the genre and it's free!

I was having a really fun time until I did a world ascension, and then I soured on it quickly. After spending many hours of unlocking a ton of Quality of Life improvements, losing all of them and being set back to square one with just a few minor boosts was enough to suck the joy right out of it. I'd say this game has about twenty hours of fun, wrapped into hundreds and hundreds of hours of re-unlocking the mechanics that make the game fun. Normally I enjoy incremental games, but this one just feels like it doesn't value my time.
